content.reply:
Got it — a food diary App: log what you ate and how much, and it fills in the calories, keeps the full history, and shows your trends. Two quick things that change how it works:

1. Should it estimate calories from your description, or do you prefer typing the number yourself?
2. Do you have a daily calorie target to compare against?

Either way you'll get fast entry, a day view with a running total, and weekly averages. One limit: it can't read photos or food labels, and it can't send you reminders — those connections aren't available yet.

interpretation.outcome: A food diary on your Mac where you log what you ate and how much, see calories per day, and watch trends over time.
interpretation.main_input: Short entries you type yourself, like "2 rotis and dal, lunch" or "large latte".
interpretation.useful_result: Today's running calorie total against your target, a searchable history of past days, and a trend of average daily calories.
important_assumptions: Calories are estimated from your description and portion, shown as an estimate you can correct.
Entries are grouped by meal: breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack.
Everything stays on this Mac and is yours to edit or delete.

build.goal: Let me log what I eat and how much through the day, see the calories, keep a full history, and understand my eating trends over time.
build.instructions:
App name for the person: My Food Diary

What success looks like: I can log a meal in a few seconds, see today's calorie total, scroll back through any past day, and see whether my average daily calories are rising or falling.

How the person will use it:
- Open the app and type what I just ate with the amount, e.g. "2 rotis and a bowl of dal", meal = lunch. -> The entry is saved with an estimated calorie figure, marked as an estimate, and today's running total updates.
- Tap the calorie figure and correct it to the number on the packet. -> The entry shows my corrected value, the estimate label is gone, totals recalculate, and I'm offered to save it as a usual food.
- Log a usual food from the shortlist. -> One tap adds it with its fixed calories per portion, with no estimate needed.
- Open history and pick last Tuesday. -> That day's entries grouped by meal with the day total, plus search across past entries by food name.
- Open trends. -> Daily totals over recent weeks, a 7-day rolling average with direction of travel, the meal split and my most frequent foods.

What it keeps:
- collection Food entries: The diary itself: one record per thing I ate, so totals, history and trends can be built from it.. Fields: Eaten at (datetime, required), Food (text, required), Amount (text, required), Quantity (number), Unit (choice), Meal (choice, required), Calories (number, required), Calories are an estimate (boolean, required), Note (text)
- collection My usual foods: Save foods I eat often with a known calorie figure per portion, so repeat logging is one tap and consistent.. Fields: Food (text, required), Portion (text, required), Calories per portion (number, required), Times logged (number)
- collection My settings: Hold optional preferences such as a daily calorie target, left empty by default.. Fields: Daily calorie target (number), Week starts on (choice)

What it does:
- action log_food: Take what I typed (food, amount, meal, optional time), fill in calories from my usual foods when it matches, otherwise from an estimate, save the entry and update today's total. (inputs: Food, Amount, Meal, Eaten at, Calories if I typed one; outputs: Saved food entry, Updated total for the day)
- action estimate_calories: From a food description and amount, produce a calorie figure plus a one-line basis, e.g. "1 roti ≈ 110 kcal". Always returned as an estimate I can overwrite. (inputs: Food, Amount, Quantity and unit if given; outputs: Estimated calories, One-line basis for the estimate)
- action correct_entry: Change the food, amount or calories of an existing entry, or remove it; clear the estimate label, recalculate the day's total and offer to save the corrected figure as one of my usual foods. (inputs: Entry to change, New values; outputs: Updated entry, Recalculated day total, Optional new usual food)
- action day_summary: For a chosen date, list entries grouped by meal and total the calories; if a daily target has been set later, also show the difference from it. (inputs: Date, Daily calorie target if set; outputs: Entries by meal, Day total, Difference from target when a target exists)
- action trends: Over a chosen period, compute daily totals, the 7-day rolling average, the direction of travel, the average split across meals and my most frequently logged foods; can be saved as a summary file. (inputs: Period; outputs: Daily totals, Rolling average and direction, Meal split, Top foods, Optional summary file)

Constraints:
- Calorie figures produced by Alpha are labelled estimates and stay editable; my own numbers are never overwritten.
- Logging a normal entry takes one screen, with nothing required beyond food, amount and meal.
- No daily target is set by default; totals show plainly until I add one.
- All entries and settings stay on this Mac, kept until I delete them.
- No entry is silently changed or deleted; history keeps what I logged.
- This is a personal food diary, not medical or dietary advice.

Agreed assumptions:
- Alpha estimates calories from your description, labelled as estimates and always editable.
- Correcting a figure clears the estimate label and offers to save it as one of your usual foods.
- No daily calorie target is set; totals show without an over/under signal until you add one.
- Only calories are recorded per entry; protein, carbs and fat can be added later.
- Days run midnight to midnight in your local timezone; weeks start Monday.
- Everything stays on this Mac and is kept until you delete it.

PLAN.md is what Alpha will check. Where it names an action, input, collection, field or label differently from the notes above, use PLAN.md's name.

Build a screen for this App (ui/src/main.tsx) using the labels PLAN.md names.

scenarios.description: Correcting an estimated figure stores my number without the estimate label, saves it as one of my usual foods, and logging that usual food again reuses the fixed calories with no estimate.
With entries on two different days, a past day and trends over a recent period can be produced without altering what was logged.
An entry with no food typed is refused and nothing is stored.
